chunks: Muhammad narrated from Ahmad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'a ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who divorces his wife while he is ill. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She inherits him as long as she is in her waiting period; and if he divorces her during the state of restlessness (marad al-maut), she inherits him up to a year. So if there is an increase upon the year by one day, she does not inherit him, and she observes the waiting period from him, for four months and ten days, the waiting period of the woman whose husband has died.'

key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا: the one who has died from her (widow)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in inheritance rules for a wife when her husband divorces her during terminal illness versus normal illness?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between general illness and the terminal phase (marad al-maut) regarding inheritance, establishing that a wife inherits for the full year of the deceased's waiting period if the divorce occurs during the critical final stage. Scholars note this ruling prevents husbands from manipulating the timing of divorce to deprive wives of their rightful inheritance share, ensuring the 'year' (hawl) applies specifically to the severe, incapacitating phase of death. The text emphasizes the precision of the one-year limit, where exceeding it by a single day reverts the inheritance to the standard three-month-and-ten-day iddah of a widow.
